raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

QSA decode and MTP target verify in Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`qwen4_exp`) attend each query row to 2,051 selected positions (512 compressed blocks of 4 tokens plus a 3-token tail). On SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell), the backend prepares them with `fused_kv_prepare`: it stores the new KV, expands the blocks and packs the selected K/V of every row into a page-strided scratch. FlashInfer's `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` then reads that scratch.

On SM120 the scratch is bf16 even when the KV pool is `fp8_e4m3`, the setting every NVIDIA recipe in the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next cookbook pins. The pack therefore writes and re-reads twice the bytes the attention needs, and at 32 or more query rows it is about 4x the cost of the attention itself.

This PR adds a JIT CUDA kernel that reads the selected fp8 K/V rows straight from the KV pool through `req_to_token`. It computes the attention in one split-K pass with no gather and no scratch. It is opt-in behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_QSA_SPARSE_DECODE_CUDA`.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/attention/qsa_sparse_decode.cuh` (new, JIT; no `sglang-kernel` release needed):
  - **Split kernel.** One CTA per (query row, KV head, split), 8 splits, 4 warps. 32-column blocks are loaded through a 2-3 stage `cp.async` pipeline. `q k^T` and `p v` run on bf16 `m16n8k16` tensor cores with an online softmax, and the kernel writes unnormalized partials. A small combine kernel then merges the 8 partials into the bf16 output.
  - **Column validity.** A column is used when `0 <= pos < seq_len` and its slot is `>= 0`. A row with no valid column outputs zeros, and blocks without a valid column are skipped.
  - **FP8 conversion.** e4m3 → bf16 is exact. The fast conversion maps the NaN codes to ±480, so a fragment containing one is converted again with `cvt` and NaN propagates.
  - **Determinism.** A row's output depends only on that row, so it is deterministic and independent of the batch.
- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/qsa_sparse_decode.py` (new): the op wrapper.
  - It picks the pipeline depth per architecture: SM12x uses 2 stages with q in registers. SM10x uses 3 stages, with q in shared memory above 32 rows; the op and its tests also run there.
  - It allocates the partials per call, so it holds no state and is CUDA-graph safe.
- `qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py`: with `SGLANG_ENABLE_QSA_SPARSE_DECODE_CUDA=1`, an `fp8_e4m3` MHA KV pool and SM120, decode and target verify skip the fused pack-for-trtllm path. They store the new KV, expand the block top-k (existing `_expand_block_indices`) and call the kernel. Otherwise nothing changes.
  - **SM100 stays on the default path.** There, upstream already packs fp8 for trtllm. The kernel measured 0.83-0.86x at 16 rows and 1.21-1.60x at 32-384 rows on GB200, so it is not enabled.
- `environ.py` + `environment_variables.mdx`: the new env var, default off, in the "Attention & Kernels" table.
- Tests: `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/qsa/test_qsa_sparse_decode.py` (`1-gpu-small`, skipped off SM100/SM120):
  - the kernel vs `qsa_sparse_attention_reference` (fp32 softmax): decode and verify rows, short and long contexts, int32/int64 request ids;
  - empty blocks and rows without a valid column;
  - determinism and batch invariance;
  - NaN propagation in K and in V;
  - CUDA-graph replay;
  - backend routing with the flag on and off.
- Benchmark: `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_qsa_sparse_decode.py` (marker `do_bench`, cold L2, CUDA graph). It compares the default path (`fused_kv_prepare` + trtllm) with store + block expansion + this kernel; both lines include the new-token KV store.

## Accuracy Tests

Outputs differ from the trtllm path at bf16 rounding level: max |diff| 9.8e-4 on the benchmark inputs. The unit tests hold the kernel to the fp32 reference at `atol=5e-3, rtol=1e-2`.

End-to-end setup:
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 with `--tp 1 --quantization modelopt_fp4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mem-fraction-static 0.93 --chunked-prefill-size 4096`, decode CUDA graphs on.
- Flag off (today's path) vs flag on, on the same GPU in the same container.
- gsm8k command: `sgl-eval run gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-threads 32 --temperature 0 --max-tokens 4096` (sgl-eval 0.1.3), server with `--max-running-requests 32 --context-length 20480 --disable-prefill-cuda-graph`.

| GPU | Checkpoint | gsm8k off | gsm8k on |
|---|---|---|---|
| RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q (300 W) | `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` | 97.00% | 97.50% |
| RTX PRO 6000 Server (600 W) | `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` | 95.50% | 97.00% |
| RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q (300 W), MTP (NEXTN 3/4) | `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` | 98.00% | 97.00% |

Across the three pairs the deltas are +0.5, +1.5 and -1.0 points: no consistent direction, all within GSM8K run-to-run variance.

Greedy outputs:
- **Requests.** 24 greedy requests of 160 tokens on 6K-20K-token prompts.
- **Upstream main is not repeat-deterministic on this model,** so the reference is main's own run-to-run agreement.
- **Without MTP:**
  - 600 W: main vs main 14/24 token-identical; flag on vs off 11/24 and 12/24.
  - 300 W: main vs main 7/24; flag on vs off 5/24 and 9/24.
- **With MTP** (NEXTN, 3 steps, 4 draft tokens; covers target verify and draft decode), 300 W: main vs main 6/24 token-identical; flag on vs off 1/24 and 4/24. On 16/24 requests main itself diverges within the first 5 tokens, so these counts are below the noise floor and do not separate the arms. The sensitive check is MTP acceptance, which is unchanged: mean accept length 2.575 (off) vs 2.569 (on) over A-B-B-A serving runs, with a run-to-run spread of up to ±0.18.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel benchmark, `python3 test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_qsa_sparse_decode.py`, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (300 W, SM120), image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261103-797af717`. Median µs per call; 24 q heads / 2 KV heads / head_dim 256, fp8 KV; both lines include the KV store of the new tokens.

| context | requests x rows/request | default (`fused_kv_prepare` + trtllm) | this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 65,536 | 16 x 1 | 42.6 | 26.2 | 1.62x |
| 65,536 | 32 x 1 | 177.7 | 43.0 | 4.13x |
| 65,536 | 64 x 1 | 413.5 | 96.0 | 4.31x |
| 65,536 | 96 x 1 | 685.7 | 159.8 | 4.29x |
| 65,536 | 4 x 4 (verify) | 42.9 | 26.1 | 1.64x |
| 65,536 | 16 x 4 | 412.9 | 86.1 | 4.80x |
| 65,536 | 32 x 4 | 903.0 | 212.4 | 4.25x |
| 65,536 | 64 x 4 | 1847.2 | 441.5 | 4.18x |
| 65,536 | 96 x 4 | 2788.8 | 687.4 | 4.06x |
| 8,192 | 16 x 4 | 377.7 | 60.8 | 6.21x |
| 8,192 | 96 x 4 | 2602.5 | 641.0 | 4.06x |

Serving, no speculative decoding, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 with fp8 KV and decode CUDA graphs, server args as above:
- **Load.** `python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 16 --seed 1`; up to 11 requests run at a time.
- **Design.** Servers in the order main, flag on, main on one GPU, 3 benchmark repetitions per server; medians over all repetitions of each arm.

| GPU | main output tok/s (6 reps) | median | flag on output tok/s (3 reps) | median | Median TPOT, main → on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q (300 W), `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` | 211.6, 222.6, 208.9, 225.2, 221.5, 222.3 | 221.9 | 226.3, 222.8, 221.7 | 222.8 (+0.4 %) | 26.80 → 26.29 ms |
| RTX PRO 6000 Server (600 W) | 223.3, 248.9, 237.4, 252.5, 250.2, 250.5 | 249.6 | 252.2, 251.7, 250.3 | 251.7 (+0.9 %) | 26.70 → 25.42 ms |

- **No end-to-end throughput gain is claimed at this load:** output throughput moves by less than main's own spread between repetitions. At 11 decode rows the kernel saves about 16 µs per QSA layer per step; the 4x kernel gains start at 32+ rows (larger decode batches, or MTP verify at 4 rows per request).
- **With MTP,** upstream sizes this GPU for 2 running requests (8 verify rows), and throughput moves only with acceptance; no gain is claimed there.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations): new env var row; no new flag, and the recommended deployment is unchanged (opt-in).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Prepared with the help of Claude Code; every result above was measured as described.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+"""QSA (Qwen4-Exp sparse attention) decode / target-verify attention over an
+FP8 E4M3 KV pool.

+``qsa_sparse_decode`` reads the K/V rows each query row selected straight from

+positions (``-1`` = hole); a column is used when ``0 <= pos < seq_lens[row]``.
+Outputs agree with the gather-then-attend path up to bf16 rounding of the
+softmax weights; they are deterministic and independent of the batch
+composition.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations

+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.arch import current_arch
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import (
+    cache_once,
+    is_arch_support_pdl,
+    load_jit,
+    make_cpp_args,
+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from tvm_ffi.module import Module
+
+_HEAD_DIM = 256
+_HEADS_PER_TILE = 16
+_NUM_SPLITS = 8
+
+
+@cache_once
+def _jit_qsa_sparse_decode_module(stages: int, q_in_smem: bool) -> Module:
+    args = make_cpp_args(stages, q_in_smem, is_arch_support_pdl())
+    return load_jit(
+        "qsa_sparse_decode",
+        *args,
+        cuda_files=["attention/qsa_sparse_decode.cuh"],
+        cuda_wrappers=[("run", f"QsaSparseDecode<{args}>::run")],
+    )
+
+
+def _launch_config(rows: int) -> tuple:
+    """(pipeline stages, q fragments in shared memory) per architecture."""
+    if current_arch().is_sm_at_least(12):
+        return 2, False
+    return 3, rows > 32
+
+
+def qsa_sparse_decode(
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    k_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    v_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    req_to_token: torch.Tensor,
+    row_req_pool_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    indices: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    sm_scale: float,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Sparse attention of each query row over its selected KV positions.
+
+    Args:
+        q: ``[rows, q_heads, 256]`` bf16.
+        k_cache, v_cache: ``[slots, kv_heads, 256]`` float8_e4m3fn KV pool
+            buffers (unit scale), with ``q_heads / kv_heads <= 16``.
+        req_to_token: ``[requests, context]`` int32 position -> slot table.
+        row_req_pool_indices: ``[rows]`` int32/int64 request of each row.
+        indices: ``[rows, topk]`` int32 logical positions, ``-1`` = hole.
+        seq_lens: ``[rows]`` int32 visible length of each row.
+        sm_scale: softmax scale.
+
+    Returns:
+        ``[rows, q_heads, 256]`` bf16.
+    """
+    rows, _, head_dim = q.shape
+    kv_heads = k_cache.shape[1]
+    if head_dim != _HEAD_DIM or k_cache.dtype != torch.float8_e4m3fn:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "qsa_sparse_decode needs head_dim 256 and a float8_e4m3fn KV cache, "
+            f"got head_dim {head_dim} and {k_cache.dtype}"
+        )
+    partials = rows * kv_heads * _NUM_SPLITS * _HEADS_PER_TILE
+    part_acc = torch.empty(partials * head_dim, dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device)
+    part_m = torch.empty(partials, dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device)
+    part_l = torch.empty(partials, dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device)
+    out = torch.empty_like(q)
+    stages, q_in_smem = _launch_config(rows)
+    _jit_qsa_sparse_decode_module(stages, q_in_smem).run(
+        q,
+        k_cache.view(torch.uint8),
+        v_cache.view(torch.uint8),
+        req_to_token,
+        row_req_pool_indices,
+        indices,
+        seq_lens,
+        part_acc,
+        part_m,
+        part_l,
+        out,
+        float(sm_scale),
+    )
+    return out

+"""Benchmark QSA (Qwen4-Exp) decode / target-verify attention over an fp8_e4m3
+KV pool, new-token KV store included.
+
+Lines:
+  - ``trtllm``: the default backend path, ``fused_kv_prepare`` (store, block
+    expansion and pack of the selected KV into a page-strided scratch) followed
+    by FlashInfer's ``trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache``.
+  - ``cuda``: ``store_cache`` + ``expand_qsa_block_indices`` + the split-K
+    ``qsa_sparse_decode`` kernel (``SGLANG_ENABLE_QSA_SPARSE_DECODE_CUDA=1``).
+
+Shape axes: ``requests`` x ``width`` query rows (width 1 = decode, 4 = verify),
+``context`` tokens per request (uniform in [context / 2, context)). Constants
+follow the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA layers at TP1: 24 q heads, 2 KV heads,
+head_dim 256, 512 selected 4-token blocks plus a 3-token tail per row.
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+import torch
+from flashinfer.decode import trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache
+from flashinfer.utils import get_trtllm_gen_multi_ctas_kv_counter_bytes
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.benchmark import marker
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.qsa_sparse_decode import qsa_sparse_decode
+from sglang.kernels.ops.kvcache.kvcache import store_cache
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.qsa.fused_kv import fused_kv_prepare
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.qsa.kernel import expand_qsa_block_indices
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_sm100_supported, is_sm120
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(
+    est_time=5, stage="base-b-kernel-benchmark", runner_config="1-gpu-large"
+)
+
+Q_HEADS, KV_HEADS, HEAD_DIM = 24, 2, 256
+RATIO, BUDGET, PAGE = 4, 2048, 64
+TOPK = BUDGET + RATIO - 1
+STRIDE = -(-TOPK // PAGE) * PAGE
+
+
+def _make_inputs(requests: int, width: int, context: int):
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(requests * 31 + width)
+    lens = torch.randint(
+        context // 2, context, (requests,), generator=gen, device="cuda"
+    )
+    pages_per_req = (lens + width + PAGE - 1) // PAGE
+    pages = int(pages_per_req.sum()) + 2
+    order = (torch.randperm(pages - 1, generator=gen, device="cuda") + 1).int()
+    req_to_token = torch.zeros(
+        requests + 1, context + 2 * PAGE, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+    )
+    start = 0
+    for r in range(requests):
+        n = int(pages_per_req[r])
+        req_to_token[r + 1, : n * PAGE] = (
+            order[start : start + n, None] * PAGE + torch.arange(PAGE, device="cuda")
+        ).flatten()
+        start += n
+    rows = requests * width
+    row_req = torch.arange(
+        1, requests + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+    ).repeat_interleave(width)
+    positions = lens.repeat_interleave(width) + torch.arange(
+        width, device="cuda"
+    ).repeat(requests)
+    num_blocks = (positions + 1) // RATIO
+    scores = torch.rand(rows, int(num_blocks.max()), generator=gen, device="cuda")
+    scores[torch.arange(scores.shape[1], device="cuda") >= num_blocks[:, None]] = -1
+    top = scores.topk(BUDGET // RATIO, dim=1)
+    fp8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    return dict(
+        k_cache=torch.randn(pages * PAGE, KV_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, device="cuda").to(fp8),
+        v_cache=torch.randn(pages * PAGE, KV_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, device="cuda").to(fp8),
+        req_to_token=req_to_token,
+        q=torch.randn(rows, Q_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+        new_k=torch.randn(rows, KV_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, device="cuda").to(fp8),
+        new_v=torch.randn(rows, KV_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, device="cuda").to(fp8),
+        loc=req_to_token[row_req.long(), positions].long(),
+        blocks=torch.where(top.values >= 0, top.indices, -1).int(),
+        seq_lens=(positions + 1).int(),
+        query_positions=positions.int(),
+        row_req=row_req,
+    )
+
+
+def _trtllm_fn(x, width):
+    rows = x["q"].shape[0]
+    packed_dtype = torch.float8_e4m3fn if is_sm100_supported() else torch.bfloat16
+    packed_k = torch.zeros(
+        rows * STRIDE, KV_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, dtype=packed_dtype, device="cuda"
+    )
+    packed_v = torch.zeros_like(packed_k)
+    counts = torch.empty(rows, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    block_tables = torch.arange(
+        rows * (STRIDE // PAGE), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+    ).view(rows, -1)
+    workspace = torch.zeros(128 * 1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    sms = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).multi_processor_count
+    counters = torch.zeros(
+        get_trtllm_gen_multi_ctas_kv_counter_bytes(rows, Q_HEADS, sms),
+        dtype=torch.uint8,
+        device="cuda",
+    )
+    kv_view = [
+        t.view(-1, PAGE, KV_HEADS, HEAD_DIM).permute(0, 2, 1, 3)
+        for t in (packed_k, packed_v)
+    ]
+
+    def fn(q, new_k, new_v, loc, blocks, seq_lens, query_positions, row_req):
+        fused_kv_prepare(
+            x["k_cache"],
+            x["v_cache"],
+            new_k,
+            new_v,
+            loc,
+            x["req_to_token"],
+            row_req,
+            blocks,
+            seq_lens,
+            counts,
+            packed_k,
+            packed_v,
+            width,
+            compress_ratio=RATIO,
+            query_positions=query_positions,
+            chain_positions=True,
+            visible_page_size=PAGE,
+        )
+        return trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache(
+            query=q,
+            kv_cache=tuple(kv_view),
+            workspace_buffer=workspace,
+            block_tables=block_tables,
+            seq_lens=counts,
+            max_seq_len=STRIDE,
+            bmm1_scale=HEAD_DIM**-0.5,
+            bmm2_scale=1.0,
+            multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer=counters,
+        )
+
+    return fn
+
+
+def _cuda_fn(x):
+    k_cache, v_cache = x["k_cache"], x["v_cache"]
+    rows = x["q"].shape[0]
+
+    def fn(q, new_k, new_v, loc, blocks, seq_lens, query_positions, row_req):
+        store_cache(
+            new_k.view(rows, -1),
+            new_v.view(rows, -1),
+            k_cache.view(-1, KV_HEADS * HEAD_DIM),
+            v_cache.view(-1, KV_HEADS * HEAD_DIM),
+            loc,
+        )
+        indices = expand_qsa_block_indices(
+            blocks, query_positions, seq_lens, RATIO, BUDGET
+        )
+        return qsa_sparse_decode(
+            q=q,
+            k_cache=k_cache,
+            v_cache=v_cache,
+            req_to_token=x["req_to_token"],
+            row_req_pool_indices=row_req,
+            indices=indices,
+            seq_lens=seq_lens,
+            sm_scale=HEAD_DIM**-0.5,
+        )
+
+    return fn
+
+
+@marker.parametrize("context", [8192, 65536], [8192])
+@marker.parametrize(
+    "requests,width",
+    [(16, 1), (32, 1), (64, 1), (96, 1), (4, 4), (16, 4), (32, 4), (64, 4), (96, 4)],
+    [(16, 1), (16, 4)],
+)
+@marker.benchmark("impl", ["trtllm", "cuda"])
+def benchmark(requests: int, width: int, context: int, impl: str):
+    x = _make_inputs(requests, width, context)
+    fn = _trtllm_fn(x, width) if impl == "trtllm" else _cuda_fn(x)
+    args = tuple(
+        x[name]
+        for name in (
+            "q",
+            "new_k",
+            "new_v",
+            "loc",
+            "blocks",
+            "seq_lens",
+            "query_positions",
+            "row_req",
+        )
+    )
+    # Selected fp8 K and V bytes: the KV a sparse decode has to read.
+    footprint = x["q"].shape[0] * TOPK * KV_HEADS * HEAD_DIM * 2
+    return marker.do_bench(
+        fn,
+        input_args=args,
+        memory_args=None,
+        memory_output=None,
+        extra_memory_footprint=footprint,
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    if not (is_sm100_supported() or is_sm120()):
+        print("[skip] QSA sparse decode benchmark requires SM100 or SM120 CUDA.")
+        sys.exit(0)
+    benchmark.run()

@@ -0,0 +1,228 @@
+"""The QSA split-K sparse decode kernel (qsa_sparse_decode) against the torch
+sparse-attention reference, plus the backend wiring behind
+SGLANG_ENABLE_QSA_SPARSE_DECODE_CUDA.
+
+Shapes follow Qwen4-Exp QSA layers: 24 q heads over 2 KV heads, head_dim 256,
+an fp8_e4m3 KV pool and top-k rows of 2048 block-expanded positions plus a
+3-token tail (-1 = hole), 1 query row per request (decode) or 4 (verify)."""
+
+import sys
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.qsa_sparse_decode import qsa_sparse_decode
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.qsa.kernel import qsa_sparse_attention_reference
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_sm100_supported, is_sm120
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not (is_sm100_supported() or is_sm120()),
+    reason="qsa_sparse_decode is tested on SM100 and SM120",
+)
+
+Q_HEADS, KV_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, PAGE, RATIO = 24, 2, 256, 64, 4
+TOPK = 2048 + RATIO - 1
+
+
+def _make_inputs(requests, width, context, seed):
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    lens = torch.randint(
+        context // 2, context, (requests,), generator=gen, device="cuda"
+    )
+    pages_per_req = (lens + width + PAGE - 1) // PAGE
+    pages = int(pages_per_req.sum()) + 2
+    order = (torch.randperm(pages - 1, generator=gen, device="cuda") + 1).int()
+    req_to_token = torch.zeros(
+        requests + 1, context + 2 * PAGE, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+    )
+    start = 0
+    for r in range(requests):
+        n = int(pages_per_req[r])
+        page_ids = order[start : start + n]
+        start += n
+        req_to_token[r + 1, : n * PAGE] = (
+            page_ids[:, None] * PAGE + torch.arange(PAGE, device="cuda")
+        ).flatten()
+    rows = requests * width
+    row_req = torch.arange(1, requests + 1, device="cuda").repeat_interleave(width)
+    seq_lens = (
+        lens.repeat_interleave(width)
+        + torch.arange(width, device="cuda").repeat(requests)
+        + 1
+    ).int()
+    slots = pages * PAGE
+    k_cache = torch.randn(slots, KV_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, generator=gen, device="cuda")
+    v_cache = torch.randn(slots, KV_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, generator=gen, device="cuda")
+    q = torch.randn(rows, Q_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, generator=gen, device="cuda")
+    blocks = (
+        torch.rand(rows, 512, generator=gen, device="cuda")
+        * (seq_lens // RATIO)[:, None]
+    ).long()
+    indices = (blocks[:, :, None] * RATIO + torch.arange(RATIO, device="cuda")).flatten(
+        1
+    )
+    tail = (seq_lens.long() // RATIO * RATIO)[:, None] + torch.arange(
+        RATIO - 1, device="cuda"
+    )
+    tail = torch.where(tail < seq_lens[:, None], tail, -1)
+    indices = torch.cat([indices, tail], dim=1)
+    indices[:, 7::97] = -1
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        q=q.bfloat16(),
+        k_cache=k_cache.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn),
+        v_cache=v_cache.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn),
+        req_to_token=req_to_token,
+        row_req=row_req,
+        indices=indices.int().contiguous(),
+        seq_lens=seq_lens,
+    )
+
+
+def _run(x, rows=slice(None)):
+    return qsa_sparse_decode(
+        q=x.q[rows],
+        k_cache=x.k_cache,
+        v_cache=x.v_cache,
+        req_to_token=x.req_to_token,
+        row_req_pool_indices=x.row_req[rows],
+        indices=x.indices[rows],
+        seq_lens=x.seq_lens[rows],
+        sm_scale=HEAD_DIM**-0.5,
+    )
+
+
+def _reference(x):
+    valid = (x.indices >= 0) & (x.indices < x.seq_lens[:, None])
+    slots = x.req_to_token[x.row_req[:, None], x.indices.clamp(min=0)]
+    slots = torch.where(valid, slots, -1)
+    return qsa_sparse_attention_reference(
+        x.q, x.k_cache, x.v_cache, slots, HEAD_DIM**-0.5
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("requests,width", [(1, 1), (3, 4), (24, 1), (8, 4), (40, 1)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("context", [300, 6000])
+def test_matches_sparse_attention_reference(requests, width, context):
+    x = _make_inputs(requests, width, context, seed=requests * 7 + width + context)
+    if width > 1:
+        x.row_req = x.row_req.int()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(_run(x), _reference(x), atol=5e-3, rtol=1e-2)
+
+
+def test_rows_without_valid_columns_and_empty_blocks():
+    """Whole 32-column blocks without a valid column are skipped before and
+    after the first valid block of a split, and a row with no valid column
+    outputs zeros."""
+    x = _make_inputs(4, 1, 300, seed=11)
+    x.indices[:, 40:300] = -1
+    x.indices[:, 340:] = -1
+    x.indices[0] = -1
+    out = _run(x)
+    assert torch.count_nonzero(out[0]) == 0
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out, _reference(x), atol=5e-3, rtol=1e-2)
+
+
+def test_deterministic_and_batch_invariant():
+    """A row's output does not depend on the run or on the other rows."""
+    x = _make_inputs(32, 4, 6000, seed=3)
+    out = _run(x)
+    assert torch.equal(out, _run(x))
+    assert torch.equal(out[20:28], _run(x, slice(20, 28)))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cache", ["k_cache", "v_cache"])
+def test_nan_in_selected_kv_propagates(cache):
+    """The fast fp8 -> bf16 conversion maps the e4m3 NaN codes to +-480;
+    fragments holding one are converted again so NaN reaches the output as
+    in the reference."""
+    x = _make_inputs(3, 4, 6000, seed=5)
+    raw = getattr(x, cache).view(torch.uint8)
+    raw[5::97, :, 17] = 0x7F
+    raw[11::89, :, 200] = 0xFF
+    out, ref = _run(x), _reference(x)
+    assert torch.isnan(ref).any()
+    assert torch.equal(torch.isnan(out), torch.isnan(ref))
+
+
+def test_cuda_graph_replay_matches_eager():
+    x = _make_inputs(16, 4, 6000, seed=9)
+    eager = _run(x)
+    _run(x)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        captured = _run(x)
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(captured, eager)
+
+
+def _fp8_backend(enabled):
+    from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+    from sglang.srt.layers.attention import qwen_sparse_attn_backend as module
+    from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp4_kv_cache_quant_method import (
+        UnquantizedKVCacheMethod,
+    )
+    from sglang.srt.mem_cache.memory_pool import MHATokenToKVPool
+
+    pool = MHATokenToKVPool.__new__(MHATokenToKVPool)
+    pool.quant_method = UnquantizedKVCacheMethod()
+    pool.dtype = torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    with envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_QSA_SPARSE_DECODE_CUDA.override(enabled):
+        backend = module.QwenSparseAttnBackend(SimpleNamespace(token_to_kv_pool=pool))
+    return module, backend
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("enabled", [False, True])
+def test_backend_routes_fp8_decode_to_kernel(monkeypatch, enabled):
+    """With the env var set on SM120, decode / verify skip the fused
+    pack-for-trtllm path and run qsa_sparse_decode on the expanded top-k;
+    without it, or on SM100, nothing changes."""
+    from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_mode import ForwardMode
+    from sglang.test.mem_cache_utils import routed
+
+    module, backend = _fp8_backend(enabled)
+    enabled = enabled and is_sm120()
+    assert backend._use_sparse_decode_cuda is enabled
+    x = _make_inputs(2, 1, 6000, seed=1)
+    backend.qsa_profile = None
+    backend.req_to_token_pool = SimpleNamespace(req_to_token=x.req_to_token)
+    backend.token_to_kv_pool = routed(
+        SimpleNamespace(
+            get_key_buffer=lambda _: x.k_cache, get_value_buffer=lambda _: x.v_cache
+        )
+    )
+    metadata = SimpleNamespace(
+        row_req_pool_indices=None, sequence_lengths=x.seq_lens, is_cuda_graph=False
+    )
+    backend._resolve_metadata = lambda _: metadata
+    marker = object()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        module, "_resolve_trtllm_sparse_decode", lambda: lambda *a, **k: marker
+    )
+    backend._forward_trtllm_sparse = lambda *args, **kwargs: marker
+    batch = SimpleNamespace(
+        forward_mode=ForwardMode.DECODE,
+        req_pool_indices=x.row_req,
+        out_cache_loc=torch.ones(2, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda"),
+    )
+    layer = SimpleNamespace(
+        layer_id=0, tp_q_head_num=Q_HEADS, head_dim=HEAD_DIM, scaling=HEAD_DIM**-0.5
+    )
+    if enabled:
+        assert (
+            backend._try_fused_kv_attention(x.q, x.q, x.q, layer, batch, x.indices)
+            is None
+        )
+    out = backend._forward_paged_attention(x.q, layer, batch, x.indices)
+    if enabled:
+        assert torch.equal(out, _run(x).reshape(2, -1))
+    else:
+        assert out is marker
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v", "-s"]))
